bib.title: From Google Gemini to OpenAI Q* (Q-Star): A Survey of Reshaping the Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) Research Landscape

read.skipped: Reference list (about lines 2678-end) skimmed, only entries cited in the body checked.

question: How do Mixture of Experts, multimodal learning and speculated AGI/Q* advances reshape the generative AI research taxonomy?
contributions: Detailed examination of the evolving landscape in generative AI, emphasizing the advancements and innovations in technologies like Gemini and Q*
Analysis of the transformative effect of advanced generative AI systems on academic research
Thorough assessment of the ethical, societal, and technical challenges arising from the integration of generative AI in academia

results.claim: DeepSpeed-MoE compression shrinks MoE model size about 3.7x and improves inference latency and cost up to 7.3x (as reported by the survey).
results.setup: MoE inference and training system; numbers quoted from the cited paper, no setup given in the survey
results.quote: decreasing the MoE model size by approximately 3.7x and optimizing inference to achieve up to 7.3x better latency and cost efficiency
results.note: Also says 'up to 3.7x while maintaining accuracy' in Sec IV-D.

results.claim: Lina cuts MoE training step time by up to 1.73x and 95th-percentile inference time by 1.63x on average against existing systems.
results.setup: Distributed MoE training/inference all-to-all bottleneck; hardware and baselines not given
results.quote: substantial reduction in training step time by up to 1.73 times and lowering the 95th percentile inference time by an average of 1.63 times

results.claim: MoE gives training cost savings of up to fivefold over dense models in some encoder-decoder cases.
results.setup: Encoder-decoder MoE vs dense, 'in certain contexts'; no model or compute stated
results.quote: cost savings of up to fivefold in certain contexts when compared to dense models

results.claim: Switch Transformer is described as having 1.6 trillion parameters.
results.setup: MoE example model named in Sec IV intro
results.note: Sec IV-D then claims 'Mixtral and Switch Transformer, with over 1.6 trillion parameters, achieved computational efficiency equivalent to a 10 billion-parameter dense model', which lumps Mixtral (8x7B) with a 1.6T model; unsupported in the survey.

results.claim: ChatGPT passed 100 million users shortly after launch.
results.setup: Commercial adoption claim, no date or count source given
results.quote: rapid adoption by over 100 million users shortly after launch

results.claim: Google Scholar listed over 55,700 entries mentioning ChatGPT within one year of commercialization.
results.setup: Google Scholar keyword search, query date not stated
results.quote: over 55,700 entries on Google Scholar mentioning “ChatGPT” within just one year

results.claim: Conversational AI and Creative AI receive the highest overall impact score (14) in the survey's own subjective 1-5 scoring against MoE, multimodality and AGI.
results.setup: Author-assigned scores, no rater protocol or inter-rater check described
results.quote: Conversational AI is marked for redirection
results.note: The scores are judgements by the authors, not measurements.

results.claim: Human Value Alignment gets the lowest overall impact score (3), rated 'inherently unresolvable' under MoE, multimodality and AGI.
results.quote: resulting in a total score of 3

results.claim: Gemini features (dual encoder, 'spike-and-slab' attention, explainability) are stated as fact but attributed to a Google source [112] or to a footnote link, with no evidence given in the survey.
results.setup: Sec I and II-B1; the survey itself says Gemini's complex-reasoning performance 'remains to be thoroughly evaluated'

results.claim: Q* is speculative: the survey's Q* capability equations are 'quasi-mathematical' formulations with no data.
results.setup: Sec V, Eq. 1-5; Q* described from press reports and a social-media post
results.quote: The corresponding quasi-mathematical formulation can be expressed as:

limits: Survey of speculation: Q* is unconfirmed and its 'capabilities' (Sec V, Eq. 1-5) are inferred from press and a tweet, with no data.
The impact scores in Table III are the authors' own judgements; no method for scoring or rater agreement is given.

Literature search is described only as key terms ('Large Language Models', 'Generative AI') across IEEE Xplore, Scopus, ACM DL, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, ProQuest, 2017-2023; no inclusion criteria or counts.
MoE numbers (3.7x, 7.3x, 1.73x, 5x) are quoted without model, hardware or baseline.
Dated: written Dec 2023, before most open MoE results; Gemini details come from the vendor report and secondary claims.
Reference [286] is cited for 'Mixtral 8x7B' but its printed title is 'Mixture-of-experts meets instruction tuning', not the Mixtral paper.
practices: Propose a hybrid peer-review model in which preprints get community review before formal review (Sec X, Fig 8).
Keep ethics and governance frameworks in step with each capability advance (Sec V-A, XI).
Use sparse fine-tuning, instruction tuning and better routing as MoE research directions (Sec IV-E).

terms.definition: replacing dense layers with sparse MoE layers comprising multiple expert networks, where a trainable gating mechanism dynamically allocates input tokens to these experts

terms.term: Emerging Direction / Requiring Redirection / Still Relevant / Likely to Become Redundant / Inherently Unresolvable
terms.definition: five impact classes scored 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 respectively for ranking how research areas are affected
